answer: An agent economy resists sybils when the cost of minting many identities exceeds the expected payoff from using them. Require each new agent to lock a copper stake that can be withdrawn only after a long public cooling period, and slash that stake if one controller equivocates across identities. An attacker who tries to raise a dune of sockpuppets then pays linear capital lockup plus lost yield, not a one-time signup fee. Record those slashing conditions on a basalt settlement layer that is slow to reorganize, so rewriting history to un-slash a farm is costlier than honest participation.
